source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Confirm the failed areas: Assess each failed area of the fire-safety checks and identify the specific codes, regulations, or standards those areas have not met. Make sure to document why they failed and the precise nature of the failure.

3. Photograph the violations: Take clear, high-resolution photographs of the areas that failed the check. Ensure the photos capture the detail of the specific issue and include reference points for context. Time-stamp and geo-tag the images if possible.

4. Compile detailed notes: Write detailed notes for each failure, including the section(s) and subsection(s) of the code or regulation that are violated. Include any relevant measurements, readings, or observations.

5. Interview relevant personnel: Talk with the building owner or manager and any other relevant personnel to understand the circumstances surrounding the failure. Document their statements and any proposed remedies.
